correctness.rationale: The first force must occur from a black vertex in one part \(V_i\), so before any color change it sees exactly the whites outside \(V_i\). Its force clears all outside whites; the remaining whites are precisely those in \(V_i\), and a now-black outside vertex can clear them exactly when their count is at most \(k\). This proves necessity and sufficiency. Maximizing whites gives \(\min\{k,n_i-1\}+\min\{k,N-n_i\}\). At the optimum, a part witnesses a minimum set exactly when its within-part white count attains the first cap, so inclusion-exclusion gives the stated count. Fresh literal dynamics checked 42,640 cases through order seven.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a compact all-set decision rule for a standard propagation process, not merely its minimum parameter, and it counts all optimum initial sets on an arbitrary complete multipartite profile. The two-part and \(k=1\) slices are established prior territory, while the arbitrary-profile structural rule and optimum multiplicity are natural reusable extensions.

final_claim: For a complete multipartite graph, an initial black set is \(k\)-forcing exactly when it is already all black or some initially black part sees between one and \(k\) white vertices outside it and leaves at most \(k\) whites in its own part; the stated closed formula for \(F_k(G)\) and inclusion-exclusion count of all minimum \(k\)-forcing sets follow.
limitations: Only the standard undirected k-forcing rule is covered; connected, PSD, oriented, probabilistic, and other forcing variants are outside scope.
